title: K Closest Points to Origin
keyIdea: Compare squared distances x² + y² (no square roots). Keep the k closest seen so far in a max-heap keyed by distance²: push each point, pop the farthest whenever the size passes k. O(n log k).

approaches.name: Your min-heap of all points
approaches.idea: Push every point into a min-heap by distance², pop k times.
approaches.why: All n points go into the heap.

approaches.name: Max-heap of size k
approaches.idea: Push {distance², index}; if size > k pop the farthest. The k left are the answer.
approaches.why: The heap never grows past k + 1.

quiz.q: Why compare x² + y² instead of the real distance?
options: Same order, no square roots needed

quiz.q: In the size-k version, why a MAX-heap for the closest points?
options: You need to throw away the farthest of the kept points, which is the max-heap's top

quiz.q: Why is your min-heap version O(n log n)?
options: It pushes all n points into the heap

quiz.q: Must the answer be sorted by distance?
